### The L3 paint steps change the canvas by a contrast the booth cannot see, and the record has never measured it
**Severity:** blocker
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/live-demo-commands-l3.txt:29-41`, `l3_report.json` `pairwise_diffs`, captures `l3v4-before.png`, `l3v4-band1_rocky.png`, `l3v4-band2_highjungle.png`, `l3v4-band3_rocky.png`
**Problem:** every paint step is accepted on a pixel-*count* diff, 1.63 to 8.84 percent, and nothing measures the *magnitude* of the change at each changed pixel. I measured it, on the identical crop (160,120,1895,855), threshold 30 on any channel. Per-pixel WCAG between the before tone and the after tone at the same coordinate, median 1.35 for `before` to `band1_rocky`, 1.64 for `before` to `band2_highjungle`, 1.47 for `pan1` to `band3_rocky`. Mean tone over the commanded stroke rectangle, before versus after, 1.015 for the Rocky Ground stroke ((34,37,13) against (39,37,17)) and 1.115 for the High Jungle stroke ((32,36,11) against (48,42,24)). Median absolute relative-luminance change per changed pixel 0.021, 0.044 and 0.031 on a 0 to 1 scale. The tone the strokes introduce, (56,44,28) at relative luminance 0.0271, sits against Jungle ground (36,44,12) at 0.0169, ratio 1.16.
**Second measurement, the change is not where the stroke is.** Of the pixels that change, only 2051 of 20723 (9.9 percent), 8078 of 97129 (8.3 percent) and 3955 of 112696 (3.5 percent) lie inside the rectangle the command list drags through, screen x 320 to 1500, screen y 360 to 392, 520 to 552 and 420 to 452. Widening to the 128x64 px brush diamond plus the stroke rows accounts for 71, 60 and 50 percent of the change. The remainder is spread across the viewport, which is the elevation-and-cliff redraw I diagnosed on 2026-11-14 at doc:1819, reappearing in a milder form.
**Failure scenario:** on 2026-11-28 the presenter drags a stroke on a 24 inch 1080p panel at 2 m. The map is Jungle World, all of whose tones I measured at WCAG 1.15 to 1.23 at doc:1903. The stroke lands on ground that already contains similar tones, the audience sees a faint darkening near terrain that was already there, and the DoD live-construction box at doc:158, "visibly change the map on the target screen while an audience watches", fails at the screen even though the injection works and the file persists.
**Contradiction surfaced, per AGENTS.md section 5:** `l3_report.json` and doc:1759 state the painted bands are plainly visible on the main canvas. They are visible as pixel counts and they are visible side by side at full resolution in my own two-up comparison of `l3v4-before.png` and `l3v4-band1_rocky.png` (`/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042/m2-l3-band1-strip.png`, the stroke row changes from green jungle to brown dirt). They are not visible as contrast at booth distance. Both statements are recorded, I did not resolve the conflict silently.
**Suggested direction, and it is a two-line change to the segment rather than a new technique.** Run the live segment on the tileset the deliverable maps are already gated on. Ice World era 6 with ground value 64 and glyph value 192 measures 6.745 dominant-tone and 6.007 worst-rendered-pair on `tux`'s own pixels, so a stroke on that pair is a change of contrast 6 rather than 1.4, and the acceptance for the re-probe is a measured per-pixel WCAG at or above 3.0 at the stroke, which I have now defined. Two prerequisites, named. First, seed the live copy from a flat Ice World map written by `build_ts.py` rather than from the Jungle River Crossing shell, so a stroke changes tone against uniform ground instead of against ground that already matches it, and so the carried-over content finding below disappears with it. Second, the palette click map in `live-demo-commands-l3.txt:24` is Jungle-specific (Water 764, Dirt 783, Mud 803, Jungle 823, Rocky Ground 843, Ruins 863, High Jungle 923) and the Ice palette row positions are not in the record and I did not measure them, so the palette coordinates must be re-derived on the target before any Ice paint step goes into the booth script. If the eight days do not stretch to that re-derive, the honest fallback is to keep Jungle, paint four or more adjacent rows per band so the change reads by area rather than tone, and state a booth viewing distance of 1 m in the run script and in the map notes.

### `tux`'s outline is truncated by the map frame and its feet do not protrude, which is why the shape reads at 64 px and not at 32
**Severity:** should-fix
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/tux.py`, parameters as recorded at doc:1782, artifacts `tux-booth64.png`, `tux-booth32.png`
**Problem, measured on my own independent re-implementation of the six ellipses.** The union touches all four map borders, head top at row 0, flipper tips at columns 0 and 255, body and feet bottom at row 255. The widest design row, 174, spans the full 256 tiles, so there is no ground margin anywhere on the silhouette's left, right or bottom. The feet do not protrude below the body, both reach row 255, and only rows 254 and 255 contain more than one silhouette run, so the foot separation is a 1 px gap in the 127 px render and vanishes at 64 px. Feature survival across the downscales, my own run-width measurement on the real pixels: rows holding two or more separated dark runs number 34 of 127 at 128 px, 16 at 64 px, 7 at 32 px. The largest internal ground gap is 21 px at 128 px, 11 px at 64 px, 5 px at 32 px. The head-to-body outline step widens from 52 px to 104 px at 128 px, 25 px to 52 px at 64 px, 12 px to 27 px at 32 px. In the mask the identity-carrying negative features are 16 tiles wide, the armpit gap at the flipper top and the two gaps flanking the body's lower tongue.
**Failure scenario:** the booth presents the whole design, which at this target means the overview thumbnail or a downscale of it. At 128 px the head step and both armpit notches are present, at 64 px they are present but thin, at 32 px they are 1 to 5 px and the figure reads as a blob with side lobes. A run script that shows the 127 px thumbnail unenlarged on a 24 inch panel puts the design at 68 mm wide and the notches at 3 mm, and a viewer at 2 m is at the edge of resolving them.
**Suggested direction, and it stays inside the single knob the builder named at doc:1802.** Inset the figure so ground survives a margin on all four sides and the feet protrude: shorten the body's vertical extent so its bottom ends above the feet's bottom, raise the head centre so its top is inside row 0, and pull the flipper centres inward so the tips sit inside the map rather than being clipped by it, keeping every positive feature above the 56-tile floor. Re-measure the run widths at 64 px and 32 px after the change, since the notches are the features that decide the verdict.

### Map 5 does not read as South Korea at booth scale without the name, and the reason is the resolution of the source outline, not the pipeline
**Severity:** blocker
**Where:** `korea-mm.png`, `korea-booth64.png`, `korea-booth32.png`, `korea-100c.png` overview render at (18,112)-(146,240), `korea.py` mask source, doc:1894 Option B
**What I read.** The 128x128 map body of `korea-100c.png` enlarged to 384 px (`/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042/m4-korea-body-3x.png`). My own correct 64 px and 32 px downscales of that body (`m4-korea-booth64-correct.png`, `m4-korea-booth32-correct.png`, enlarged with nearest neighbour for reading). The published `korea-booth64.png` and `korea-booth32.png`. A side-by-side of the map mask against my own independent rasterization of the upstream ring (`m4-korea-mask-vs-geo.png`), which are visually indistinguishable, consistent with the 95.86 percent IoU.
**What I see.** At 128 px, a filled mass whose northern boundary rises from a shoulder in the west to a point just east of centre and then falls steeply to the east, an indented west coast with two steps, a smooth rounded east side, a south end tapering to a blunt tail, and one detached small ellipse below the west end. Nothing in that description is uniquely Korean. The features that make Korea recognizable at a glance, the deeply indented south-west coast with its bays, the south-east bulge around Busan, the narrow neck at Pohang, and Ulleungdo, are all absent, because the source ring has 18 vertices over a 4.22 by 3.35 degree box. At 64 px the mass is 30 x 47 px and the detached body is 7 x 4 px. At 32 px the mass is 15 x 23 px and the detached body is 3 x 2 px, and I cannot read either as a country.
**Failure scenario:** on 2026-11-28 the presenter opens `republic-of-korea.scm`, shows the overview thumbnail, and says nothing. A visitor at the booth, including a Korean visitor at a Seoul conference, looks at the silhouette on the screen and cannot say which country it is. The DoD rows at doc:171 and doc:172, each map "described by what a player sees" and its design intent carried by a technique that works, are then met only by narration, and the legibility gate box at doc:174 is not met at all, because an independent reader of the artifact cannot identify the intended picture. The other four maps pass this test, `tux` at 64 px, the heart at 32 px, the Rocky disc at 32 px, "FOSS for All" at 4x. Map 5 is the one that does not.
**Suggested direction, ranked, and the first one is cheap.** 1. Re-rasterize from a higher-resolution ring, Natural Earth 50 m or 10 m South Korea, which carries the south-west bays and the south-east coast, and gate it on the same four numbers. My measured 10-tile floor means a feature must be at least 10 tiles wide to have any chance at 64 px, and 20 tiles to read at 32 px, so the ring has to be filtered at that floor rather than simplified to 18 vertices. This is a mask data change against the same pipeline, one dispatch, seven days. 2. If that cannot be afforded, keep the current mask and record map 5's disposition honestly: the silhouette is a coarse, geographically correct outline whose identifiability depends on the name being shown, which makes finding 6 a prerequisite rather than a nicety. 3. Do not attempt to fix recognizability by adding marks inside the shape. That is the two-tone internal feature class this task already excluded at doc:84 and doc:2206.

### Map 5's outline carries no coastal feature at all, so the recorded 10-tile coastal floor is met by absence rather than by design
**Severity:** should-fix
**Where:** `republic-of-korea_report.json`, `korea.py`, doc:84, doc:2107, `## Next Actions` doc:210 "coastal features at 10 tiles or larger"
**Problem, measured on the mask in the published file.** Rows containing two or more separate glyph runs: **1 row out of 256**. Largest ground gap enclosed between two glyph runs in the same row: **8 tiles**. Enclosed ground tiles: 0. Narrowest glyph run in any row: 2 tiles, and that is the taper of the shape's northern point at row 11, not a coastal feature. The width profile of the mainland is 2 tiles at row 11, 62 at 31, 101 at 51, 111 at 91, 115 at 111, 108 at 131, 102 at 151, 81 at 171, 38 at 191, a broad body tapering to a point in the north-east and to a narrow tail in the south. There is no bay, no inlet, no strait and no peninsula in the silhouette, because an 18-vertex 110 m outline removes all of them from a coastline that in reality has many.
**Failure scenario:** the acceptance line recorded at doc:210 says coastal features are 10 tiles or larger. A reader takes that to mean the map shows a articulated coast, and the map in fact shows a smooth coast with no articulation, which is the single biggest reason a Korean visitor at the booth may not read the silhouette as Korea. The claim is technically true and misleading in effect, and the record should say which.
**Suggested direction:** restate the design intent as "coarse filled outline from a 110 m 18-vertex simplification, no coastal features", and if coastal articulation is wanted, it has to come from a higher-resolution ring (Natural Earth 50 m or 10 m) rather than from adding marks by hand. That is a mask data change, not a pipeline change, and it is testable in one pass against the same gate.

### The rebuilt map reads as Korea at 128 px from shape alone, and at 64 px as a peninsula with an island, which is the gate the `M4` build failed
**Severity:** nit, verdict recorded
**Where:** `republic-of-korea-mm.png`, `republic-of-korea-booth64.png`, `republic-of-korea-booth32.png`, `m6-read-mm-3x.png`, `m6-read-booth64-4x.png`, `m6-64px-old-vs-new.png` under `/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042`
**What I read first, before measuring.** The 128x128 body enlarged 3x with nearest neighbour. A tall landmass, broad across the north, a ragged upper edge with a peak just right of centre, the north side falling steeply and smoothly to the east. The **west coast carries a deep inlet complex at mid-west** with two distinct notches and stepped land between them. The east coast is convex and mostly smooth with one notch at mid-east. The **south coast is serrated**, a fringe of small land pieces and gaps rather than a line. One detached elongated island sits below the south-west, wider than tall. A white rectangle in the top-left corner, which is the editor viewport indicator and not map content. The features that make Korea recognizable at a glance, the indented south-west coast, the articulated south coast, the detached island, and the smooth east side against the indented west, are present. I read it as the Korean peninsula from shape alone.
**What I see at 64 px.** My dark-pixel census of the published `booth64` gives exactly **two** connected bodies: the mass at 994 px in a 32x48 px box, and the island at 21 px in a 7x5 px box. 11 rows carry two or more runs, 69 runs in total. The peninsula-plus-island-off-the-south-west gestalt survives, the west inlet is visible as a notch, and the south fringe survives as texture. At 128 px the same census gives 4 bodies, mass 3873 px in 62x96, island 74 px in 14x8, the eastern island 16 px in 5x7, 36 multi-run rows, 184 runs.
**Measured comparison against the build it replaces, my own 64 px renders from the same measured body rectangle.** New mass 32x48 px with 11 multi-run rows. Old mass 30x47 px, and my mask decimation gives **13 rows with two or more runs at 64 px on the new mask against 0 on the old**, 34 against 1 at 128 px, 0 against 0 at 32 px. At 32 px the new render is 15x23 px with a 3x2 px dot, 1 multi-run row. That is the recorded out-of-scope bound, and I record it for this map rather than leaving it inherited from `tux`.
**Honest limit on this verdict.** I knew the intended subject before I opened the images, and I cannot un-know it, so this is not a blind test. What I did instead was name the features that carry the identification and check that they are geography rather than artefact. My own independent sea-anchor test, 14 anchors of my own choosing at my own approximate coordinates with an 11x11 tile window (about 12.5 km half-width, which absorbs my own coordinate error of a few km): **9 of 14 gain sea tiles, 5 of them by 15 or more** (Incheon 0 to 52, Ganghwa Strait 0 to 35, Gangjin Bay 0 to 23, Gwangyang Bay 0 to 47, Namhae Strait 44 to 62 tiles), the others by smaller amounts (Seosanman head 11 to 16, Geum estuary 0 to 4, Pohang neck 22 to 23, Busan coast 75 to 78), **3 lose it** (Asan Bay 10 to 4, Mokpo 58 to 39, Donghae inlet 50 to 44), and 2 hold, one of which is Jinhae at 0 sea tiles in both masks, where my own anchor coordinate lands on land in both and so tests nothing, and the other is Ulleungdo's position at 110 of 121 tiles sea in both, which matches the recorded absence. The bays are real. **Residual risk stated plainly:** a visitor with no priming may read the 64 px artifact as "a peninsula with an island" rather than as Korea specifically. The 128 px overview render is where the coast carries it, so the booth should present the overview thumbnail, not only a 64 px artifact.
**Suggested direction:** none for the map. For the booth script, present this map at the overview thumbnail, which `M5` measures at 0.5 px per tile, and not at a 64 px artifact, because the difference in this map's identifiability is carried by features between 1 and 4 px at 64 px.

### The recorded 10-tile floor is not reproducible from the record as written, and the shipped mask only reproduces under a minimum-dimension reading
**Severity:** should-fix
**Where:** doc:2009 "Then the recorded 10-tile component floor drops 28 components totalling 210 tiles", doc:106 "coastal features kept at roughly 10 tiles or larger", `republic-of-korea_report.json` `new_mask.components_8conn`, `m5_raster.py` `apply_feature_floor`
**My measurement.** I rasterized the upstream 10 m feature myself: 1 feature, MultiPolygon, **53 rings, 3060 coordinate pairs, 3007 distinct vertices**, all rings closed, bbox lon 124.613617 to 131.862522 and lat 33.197577 to 38.624335, largest ring 1593 pairs. My 4x4 point-sampled even-odd fill at the recorded projection gives **15928 tiles, 24.30 percent, 34 components**. IoU against the shipped mask **0.9454**. So the shipped mask is the upstream geometry at the recorded projection, confirmed without the builder's code, the same kind of check I ran on the 110 m build at doc:2507. The floor is where the record becomes unreproducible. Applying the floor as **area of 10 tiles or more** keeps **9 components, 15825 tiles** (it keeps Ulleungdo, which I rasterize at 12 tiles in a 4x4 box at cols 247-250 rows 58-61). Applying it as **minimum dimension 10 tiles or more** keeps exactly **3 components, 15701 tiles**, which is the shipped component census `15467 + 296 + 68`, at IoU **0.9517**. My drop count under the dimension reading is **31 components, 227 tiles**, against the recorded 28 components and 210 tiles.
**Failure scenario:** a reader who re-runs this pipeline from the record, reading "10 tiles or larger" as area, ships 9 components instead of 3, including Ulleungdo, and the map they ship is not the map this read certified. `Vector` cannot reproduce the shipped mask from the documentation as written.
**Suggested direction:** name the rule as a minimum-dimension floor in `korea_10m.apply_feature_floor` and in the report, restate the dropped count under that rule, and keep Ulleungdo's absence stated the way `M5` already states it, as a consequence of the floor rather than an omission. The 3-component, 227-tile difference between my fill and the builder's fill is expected from a different sampling rule and does not need reconciling, but the floor definition does.

### Two wording nits in the `M5` record that a reader would reproduce wrongly
**Severity:** nit
**Where:** doc:2030 landmarks, `republic-of-korea_report.json` `new_mask.runs` and `old_mask.runs`
**Problem.** First, doc:2030 records "Jeju 29 tiles wide becoming 25 tiles". My measurement of the shipped mask gives the Jeju component bbox **29 columns wide** (x79-107, 17 rows tall, 296 tiles) and its **widest single run 25 tiles**. Both numbers are right and they describe different things, so the sentence reads as if the island shrank in width when it shrank in its widest run. Second, the report's `runs` field is 277 for the new mask and 2 for the old one. My count of all glyph runs over occupied rows is 405 for the new mask and 204 for the old, over 209 and 203 occupied rows. 277 and 2 are exactly the runs counted **only in rows that already have two or more runs**, which I verified by computing both readings. The key name does not say that.
**Failure scenario:** a reader recomputing the articulation claim counts runs over all rows, gets 405, and reports a 128-run discrepancy against the report, or reads 277 against my 405 as a defect in the mask rather than in the definition.
**Suggested direction:** state the denominators, "runs within multi-run rows" and "Jeju widest run 25 tiles, bbox 29 wide".

### Dispatch M8, `i-love-korea`, independent read (`Shadow`, 2026-11-21)

**What this read ran on.** My own scripts `/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042/m8_mask.py`, `m8_render.py`, `m8_legibility.py` and `m8_fixsim.py`, outputs `m8_mask.json`, `m8_render.json`, `m8_legibility.json`, `m8_fixsim.json`. No builder module is imported by any of them, and no builder measurement is quoted as evidence for a number below. `chkdump` (StormLib, MIT) is used for one thing, decompressing `i-love-korea.scm`; the chunk walk, the `MTXM` decode, the mask, the coverage, the geometry, the tone census, the contrast, the decimation-rule test and the stroke sweep are my code. Inputs are the shipped `i-love-korea.scm`, `i-love-korea.chk`, `i-love-korea-mm.png`, `i-love-korea-booth64.png`, `i-love-korea-booth32.png`, `m7-open.png`, `m7-reopen.png`, `m7-jump.png`. No target contact.

**What I saw before I measured, stated as seeing.** At the 128x128 body crop I read a serifed capital `I`, a solid heart, then five letter-shaped forms, each one a tall column of dark vertical strokes with lighter interiors. At 64 px the `I` and the heart stay dark and solid, and after the heart the row collapses into a comb of alternating dark stripes on grey with character-sized separations, the thin strokes visibly lighter than the heart and none of the closed shapes closed. At 32 px it is a bar, a heart, and a striped block. That description came from reading the three published images before any script ran.

**Criterion I set before measuring, and it is mine.** Ground tone is the dominant tone of the map body I located, [176,176,176]. A pixel is INK when its WCAG contrast against that ground tone is 3.0 or better, which is this task's own gate value, FAINT between 1.5 and 3.0, and OFF below 1.5. An element reads when INK pixels appear on at least 80 percent of its vertical extent and the INK area is at least 50 percent of the area its own `MTXM` footprint implies at that resolution. The 80 and 50 percent shapes match `M7`'s so the two reads are comparable, and the ink definition differs on purpose, contrast against ground rather than a tone classifier.

**The pipeline numbers I reproduce independently.** `chkdump` extraction 614210 B, SHA-256 `5dda6941018958c854ee4aee7426f28e4a65e0d7505c6aa87270d53272f153c0`, byte-identical to the published `i-love-korea.chk`. My own chunk walk finds `VER `, `IVER`, `VCOD`, `IOWN`, `OWNR`, `ERA `, `DIM `, `SIDE`, `MTXM` 131072 B, `PUNI`, `UPGR`, `PTEC`, `UNIT` 0 B, `ISOM` 265224 B, `TILE` 131072 B, `STR `, `MRGN` 1280 B, no `DOOD`. `MTXM` low bytes give 65536 tiles, distinct values exactly {64, 192}, value 192 covers 19666 tiles, coverage **30.01 percent**, my own perimeter 5082 edges, matching the reported figure. Mask bbox rows 9 to 246 and columns 8 to 247, so glyph height **238 tiles** with margins 9 rows top and bottom and 8 columns left and right. My own column segmentation gives seven elements, widths 15, 70, 25, 25, 25, 25, 25 tiles, gaps 5 tiles each, and the thinnest horizontal glyph run inside every letter is **5 tiles** while the thinnest vertical run is 34. Element tile counts, mine, `I` 1870, heart 3516, `K` 2380, `O` 2720, `R` 3060, `E` 3060, `A` 3060. Element glyph tiles divided by element widths give a font cell of **5 tiles wide by 34 tall**, and the row spends 48 cells: 3 for the `I`, 14 for the heart, 5 for each letter, 1 gap each. Those cell figures come out of the shipped mask, not out of `glyph.py`.

### The row does not read at the certified 64 px bound as shipped, and three of seven letterforms fall below this task's own contrast gate
**Severity:** blocker
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/i-love-korea-booth64.png`, per-element census in `/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042/m8_legibility.json` `booth64_elements`
**Problem.** At the 64 px thumbnail-class artifact this task certifies, `I`, `O` and `E` do not hold 3.0 contrast against the ground tone over their own extent, and at 128 px all seven do, so the map is fine in the editor and the failure is specific to the 4x artifact class.
**What I measured.** Whole-artifact census against ground: 865 px at 3.0 or better (21.12 percent), 565 px between 1.5 and 3.0 (13.79 percent), 2666 px below 1.5 (65.09 percent, which is the ground itself), darkest pixel in the artifact 8.832 against ground. Per element, ink area as a percentage of the element's own mask footprint and ink rows as a percentage of its visible extent: `I` 53.0 percent and 16 of 60 rows (26.7 percent), heart 96.5 percent and 16 of 18 (88.9), `K` 67.9 and 59 of 60 (98.3), `O` 29.4 and 17 of 60 (28.3), `R` 82.6 and 59 of 60 (98.3), `E` 60.7 and 28 of 60 (46.7), `A` 86.8 and 59 of 60 (98.3). Four read, three do not, reached with a classifier that shares nothing with `M7`'s and landing on the same three letters. On the 128 px body crop the same criterion gives every element 88.6 to 100.3 percent of its implied area as INK with INK on 118 or 119 of its own extent rows, that is 100 percent row coverage for all seven, and the crop carries exactly three colours, ground 11764 px, glyph [36,40,56] 4546 px, white 74 px, with the glyph-to-ground pair at **WCAG 6.745** by my own luminance calculation.
**Failure scenario:** `S1` lists `i-love-korea` as an accepted map because it passed coverage, contrast and re-open, and the booth shows the 64 px thumbnail where `O` holds 29.4 percent of its own ink and covers a quarter of its height. A visitor sees `I`, a heart, and a striped block, and the map that was added on the operator's own instruction is the one that fails to say the thing it was built to say.
**Suggested direction:** rebuild at a stroke width the measurement says survives, see the finding on the stroke sweep below. This map is not blocked, it is unaccepted as shipped.

### SCMDraft's overview thumbnail is a top-left point sample, proven at 16384 of 16384 px, and that is the mechanism that decides every map design in this task
**Severity:** should-fix, travels to `S1`, `V1` and every later map build
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/i-love-korea-mm.png` against my own mask decode, test and result in `/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042/m8_fixsim.json` `decimation_rule_matches_of_16310`
**What I measured.** The 128x128 body is a hard two-tone image, three colours and no blends, so the editor does not area-average when it decimates 256 tiles to 128 px. I tested candidate rules against the real crop. Sampling the **top-left tile of each 2x2 block** matches 16384 of 16384 non-overlay pixels. The next best candidate, bottom-left tile, matches 16096; `all_of_4` 16032; majority-of-four 15316; any-of-four 15289. Applying the winning rule to my own mask reproduces the published crop with **0 px differing**, and it predicts 4554 glyph px against the 4546 the crop contains, the 8 px gap being exactly the overlay in the finding below. This closes the question `M7` named at doc:2096 as a check that did not run, whether the thumbnail decimation is nearest or majority sampling.
**Failure scenario:** a designer reads coverage 30.01 percent and assumes a 5-tile stroke is 1.25 px of a 64 px artifact and will average to a visible mid-tone. It does not. The thumbnail first throws away half the tiles by point sampling, so a 5-tile stroke enters the 128 px render as a 2.5 px band whose position depends on tile parity, and the Lanczos step after that has nothing solid to blend. Any feature under 2 tiles is absent from the editor thumbnail outright, and this task has never stated that number as a design floor.
**Suggested direction:** record the sampling rule as a measured constant beside the panel rectangle `M6` recorded, and state the design floor it implies, 6 tiles for a stroke at the 64 px bound, in the brief of any map dispatch that has letterforms or thin features in it.

### The stroke measurement points at a single row at 6-tile strokes with the heart capped at 6 cells, not at fewer characters and not first at a two-line layout
**Severity:** should-fix, this is the fix direction the numbers support
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042/m8_fixsim.json` `stroke_sweep` and `layout_options`
**What I measured.** I thicken the shipped mask by dilation only, no font re-render and no builder code, run it through the proven pipeline (top-left sample to 128 px, then single-step Lanczos to 64), and measure with the same criterion. Stroke 5 tiles reproduces the shipped pattern, simulated row coverage 28.3 for the `I` against 26.7 measured on the real artifact, 28.3 for `O` against 28.3, 46.7 for `E` against 46.7, seven elements still separate. Stroke 6 passes on all seven, ink 87.8 to 128.3 percent of the shipped footprint, ink on 98.3 percent of extent rows for all six letterforms and 88.9 for the heart, the six inter-element gaps still hold, and the enclosed counters survive, `O` 15 tiles wide becoming 13, which is 3.25 px at 64 px. Stroke 7 also passes with counters at 11 tiles. Symmetric thickening at 8 and 10 tiles merges the row into one element, because the gaps are 5 tiles, so uniform thickening is not a route. The budget arithmetic from the measured 48-cell row at 8-tile ground margins, from `m8_fixsim.json`, is that at `S_X` 6 the row has 40 cells and leaves 6 cells, 36 tiles, for the heart. At `S_X` 7 it leaves 0.29 cells and does not fit. At `S_X` 8 `KOREA` alone is 29 cells of the 30 available, so a single row at 8-tile strokes is impossible. Two lines at `S_X` 8 and `S_Y` 16 fit, 15 rows available against 15 needed, letters 112 tiles tall, 28 px at 64 px, strokes 8 tiles, 2 px.
**What it costs, stated so the choice is visible.** At `S_X` 6 the letters stay 238 tiles, 59.5 px at 64 px, which is what the operator's "very big writing" asked for, and the heart becomes 36 tiles wide, about 9 px at 64 px. A filled mass survives that, measured, the shipped heart holds 96.5 percent of its implied ink at 64 px and 96.5 percent even in the 32 px artifact, so the heart is only load-bearing as a mass, never as a stroke. The two-line option keeps a large heart and gets 2 px strokes but halves letter height to 28 or 30 px, a weaker answer to the same instruction, so it ranks second. Fewer characters is not what the numbers point at, because seven elements fit at 6-tile strokes.
**Failure scenario:** a rebuild keeps the single row and simply enlarges the heart, `S_X` stays 5, and the sweep result for stroke 5 repeats, because the heart was never the failing element.

### The editor's viewport-indicator overlay overwrites glyph ink inside the published body crop, and it is carried into both booth artifacts
**Severity:** should-fix
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/i-love-korea-mm.png` rows 0 to 11, columns 0 to 26, and everything derived from it, `i-love-korea-booth64.png`, `i-love-korea-booth32.png`, `i-love-korea-mm-2x.png`
**What I measured.** The crop has exactly three colours. The third is pure white, 74 px, forming a solid rectangle 12 rows by 27 columns at the top-left corner of the body, which is SCMDraft's viewport indicator drawn over the map render. I tested those 74 positions against my own mask: **8 of them sit where the map has glyph tiles** and 66 over ground. The visible consequence is on the leftmost letter, the `I`. Its top serif reads 0, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 0 glyph px across its eight sampled rows while its bottom serif reads 8 on all eight rows, so the top serif is short at both ends in the crop and in every artifact made from it. The overlay's own contrast against the ground tone is **2.169**, below this task's 3.0 gate, so a below-gate element is present in an artifact recorded as chrome-free. `M7` disclosed the 0.45 percent at doc:2085, which is why this is a should-fix and not a concealment finding. No capture in this set avoids it, `m7-jump.png` puts the indicator at rows 57 to 68, columns 49 to 76, covering 14 mask-glyph positions, worse than the open render.
**Failure scenario:** the booth artifact shows a pale box fused to the top of the `I`, and a reader comparing `i-love-korea-mm.png` against the map finds the serif asymmetric and cannot tell whether the design or the capture caused it. At `S_X` 6 in a rebuild the `I` narrows, so a fixed capture matters before the next artifact set is cut, not after.
**Suggested direction:** take the overview capture with the viewport parked where the indicator lands entirely in the ground margin, and record the indicator rectangle and its map position in the report the way the body rectangle is recorded. If no park position clears the glyph, state in the artifact table that the overlay is part of the published crop and name the px it covers.

### `M7`'s level (a) survival measurement runs a pipeline the published artifact does not take, and on its own it reads all seven letterforms surviving
**Severity:** nit
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/i-love-korea_report.json` `survival_4x_mask_lanczos` against `survival_4x_real_booth64`
**What I measured.** Level (a) resamples the shipped mask 256 to 64 in a single Lanczos step and reports all 7 components surviving, `I` at 133.5 percent of expected ink and vertical coverage 1.0. The real artifact is point-sampled 256 to 128 by the editor first, then Lanczos to 64, and on that path the same `I` measures 0.53 of expected ink and 0.267 vertical coverage, which is what my independent census reproduces at 53.0 percent and 26.7 percent. `M7` labelled the three levels separately and used the real path for its conclusion, so nothing is wrong here, but the record is quotable in pieces.
**Failure scenario:** a later dispatch, `S1` or `V1`, quotes `components_after_4x_8conn = 7` from level (a) as evidence that a 5-tile stroke survives 4x, designs the next map on it, and the real artifact fails the way this one did.
**Suggested direction:** one sentence beside each level naming the pipeline it measures, mask-only Lanczos versus editor-sample-then-Lanczos, and keep the real-path figures as the ones a gate decision is taken from.

### Legibility at 128 px, at 64 px, and at 32 px, with my criterion stated and my numbers attached
**Severity:** should-fix, one element short at the 64 px bound
**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/i-love-korea-2line-booth64.png`, `i-love-korea-2line-booth32.png`, my census in `/tmp/opencode/shadow-t0042/m10_ink.json`
**Criterion I am using, stated so it can be argued with.** For each element, ideal ink is the element's mask tile count scaled to the artifact (at 64 px, tiles x 0.0625), and rendered ink is pixels classified glyph tone (within 40 of `(36,40,56)` and closer to glyph than to ground). Pass is ink ratio 90 percent or better. Mid-tone share of the element box is reported alongside because mid-tone is the signature of a stroke that has been blended rather than drawn.
**At 128 px, the real editor overview render.** Ink ratio 100 percent for all seven elements, `I` 352 of 352, heart 2109 of 2110, `K` 448, `O` 512, `R` 576, `E` 576, `A` 576, mid-tone 0.0 percent everywhere, extent rows carried 56 of 56 for every letter and 53 of 54 for the heart. **My visual read at that size, `m10-reb-thumb128-2x.png`: an `I` with serifs top and bottom, a filled heart with two lobes and a point, and capitals `KOREA` on a second line, counters open in `O`, `R` and `A`, all seven separable.** The row reads.
**At 64 px, the certified thumbnail-class bound.** `I` **43.2 percent** ink (38 of 88 ideal px, 40.3 percent mid-tone), heart 94.4, `K` 98.2, `O` 93.8, `R` 96.5, `E` 95.8, `A` 97.2. Six of seven pass my criterion. `I` does not, its 8-tile stem is 2 px at 0.25 px/tile and the resize blends it into mid-tone, while its 24-tile serifs render 6 px wide and carry. **My visual read at 64 px, `m10-reb-booth64-4x.png`, is still `I`, a heart, and `KOREA`.** So the honest split is that the row reads as a message while one element does not carry its own ink, and the failing element is the `I`'s stem, not a letter whose identity is lost.
**At 32 px.** `K` renders 0 glyph pixels against 28 ideal, mid-tone 73.8 percent, other elements 25.0 to 88.7 percent. Consistent with the 32 px bound already recorded out of scope for `tux` and `republic-of-korea`, and unchanged for this map.
**Apples-to-apples against the shipped build under the same criterion and my own artifact provenance.** Shipped at 128 px, 88.6 to 100.3 percent, reads. Shipped at 64 px, heart 91.9, `R` 73.7, `E` 54.4, `A` 47.6, `I` 43.6, `K` 35.0, `O` 25.9. Mean ink ratio 53.2 percent, against 88.4 percent for the rebuild (96.0 excluding `I`).
**Disagreement with `M8`, kept rather than resolved, per AGENTS.md section 5.** `M8` at doc:3154 recorded `K`, `R`, `A` and the heart passing and `I`, `O`, `E` failing at 64 px, with `O` at 29.4 percent. My model-free ranking puts `O` last at 25.9 percent (agreement) but puts `K` at 35.0 percent and `A` at 47.6 percent, which fails two elements `M8` recorded as passing. ### Ruling, which build is the right booth answer on the main canvas
**The two-line 112-tile build at `16fe455d46fd...` is the right booth answer, and the shipped 238-tile single row at `82589b4205f5...` stays superseded.** The reason is framing, not stroke subtense, and it is arithmetic on measured quantities. At the 25 percent floor the viewport is 214 x 94 tiles. The rebuild's line 1, `I` then heart, is 150 x 112 tiles, 1200 x 896 px, which **fits the viewport width entirely** and overflows its height by 18 tiles, so one frame carries rows 8 to 94, 87 of the 112 rows, and one vertical pan completes it. Line 2, `KOREA`, is 232 x 112 tiles, 1856 x 896 px, and overflows the width by 18 tiles, so it needs two horizontal frames, exactly what `m9-jump.png` shows, its `K` clipped at the left edge of the canvas and its `A` clipped at the right. The shipped row is 240 x 238 tiles, 1920 x 1904 px, which is the panel's own width and 2.5 times the viewport height. At the floor a frame carries 94 of its 238 rows, **39.5 percent of a letter's height**, and to frame one whole letter needs 3.16 px/tile, 9.9 percent zoom, 2.5 times below the floor. No permitted zoom of the shipped build shows a whole letterform, only slices, so its 5-tile strokes being large is beside the point. The counter-reading kept at doc:16, that a panned shipped stroke is 160 px and 28.33 mm at 100 percent zoom, is arithmetically right and does not rescue the framing, a 28 mm stroke through a 133 mm viewport is still a slice of a 337 mm letter.
**Residual, stated as a measured option and not as a demand.** Even the rebuild cannot frame a whole line at the floor, 112 tiles against 94. A layout at letter box 36 tiles wide by 94 tall with the same 8-tile strokes and 8-tile gaps would make line 2 212 tiles wide and 94 tall, which fits one 25 percent frame whole in both axes at the same 11.33 mm stroke, so the legibility cost is zero and the gain is one frame instead of four for `KOREA`. It is a re-parameterisation of the same pipeline, and with five days left the cost is one build, one capture and one read. I am not dispatching it and I am not calling the current rebuild inadequate, the current rebuild reads.

On the 25 percent main canvas I measure five tones in the map region, ground `(176,176,176)` and `(164,164,168)`, glyph `(36,40,56)`, `(32,32,44)`, `(28,28,44)`, plus black tile-boundary lines. My worst glyph-against-ground pair there is **5.889**, `(164,164,168)` against `(36,40,56)`, and the two ground tones sit **1.145** apart, which is the editor's own tile banding at 8 px/tile and is what makes a 64 px stroke read as eight dark bands separated by black grid lines. All measured pairs are above the 3.0 gate. **Failure scenario:** a reader treats four printed 6.745 figures as four independent confirmations, as happened with maps 2 and 3 at doc:2746. **Suggested direction:** report the worst pair per artifact and name the tile-boundary tones once.
2. The heart's bottom apex row is absent from the 128 px render, my extent check carries 53 of 54 rows. The apex is a 1-tile-wide row and the thumbnail's 2x2 top-left point sample does not sample it. **Failure scenario:** a reader compares the thumbnail against the map, finds the point 1 tile shorter, and suspects the writer. **Suggested direction:** record it as a property of the proven point-sample rule, not as a mask or writer defect.

**Verdict on the gate question this dispatch was staged to answer.** At the real whole-map overview render, 128 px, **an unaided viewer reads `I`, a heart, and `KOREA`**, my ink ratio is 100 percent on all seven elements with mid-tone 0.0 percent, and my visual read resolves all seven shapes. At the certified 64 px bound **the row still reads as a message**, my visual read at 64 px is `I`, heart, `KOREA`, six of seven elements hold 93.8 to 98.2 percent of their ink, and `I` does not, at 43.2 percent with 40.3 percent of its box blended to mid-tone because its 8-tile stem is 2 px at that scale. 32 px is out of scope on the already recorded bound and my numbers are consistent with it. The booth crop is **genuinely chrome-free against the viewport-indicator overlay for the published artifacts**, 74 overlay px all on ground, 0 on glyph, and an inpaint control that moves no element by more than 3.4 points, and it is **not chrome-free for the 25 percent and overview-jump captures**, where 33 and 102 overlay px sit on glyph cells. On the main canvas at the editor's reachable floor of 25 percent, 8.00 px/tile, 214 x 94 tiles, 1.417 mm/tile, the two-line build is the right booth answer and the shipped single row is not, because the shipped build cannot show a whole letterform at any zoom the editor reaches. `i-love-korea` is therefore **booth-accepted in the `M9` two-line form at `16fe455d46fd...`, with the `I` element recorded as the known weak point at the 64 px thumbnail bound**, and `S1` presents it at 25 percent rather than 100 percent.

**Control limit on this read, stated as it was in `M4`, `M6` and `M8`.** I knew the intended row before I looked. This read proves that the letterforms carry or do not carry, and that the framing arithmetic holds, it does not prove that a reader who has never opened this doc would supply the word. ### R1 independent read of the booth capture sets and the P1 captures, and the ruling on the 2026-11-14 versus 2026-11-22 Flatpak Wine conflict (2026-11-22, `Shadow`, first reader in this review chain)

**What I read in this doc.** `## Status` only, plus the section-boundary lines at doc:4344 to doc:4354, which I needed as the anchor for this write. Nothing else in this doc was read, so I have no `## Plan`, `## Implementation`, `## Security` or `## Test Results` context, and this read is a first read of the artifacts, not a re-read of anyone's.

**Sampling rule, stated before selection.** Three rules, applied mechanically. First, for the published booth record, read the newest full six-map cycle whose captures are actually in the repo, which is the `S1b300L1` set (52 frames), and read every `*-open.png` in it, one per map plus the scratch map, because the open frame is the frame the runbook's `open` step produces (`BOOTH-RUNBOOK.md:105`). Second, for the published-mode run that `S1c` measured, read the controller-side `S1c300L1` set by the same rule, every `*-open.png`, plus two representative content frames chosen by alphabetical position, `S1c300L1-i-love-korea-open.png` and `S1c300L1-tux-f3.png`. Third, for the certified thumbnail class, read every file matching `booth-artifacts/*booth64.png` numerically and read visually the two artifacts of the same map whose names differ only by prefix, `korea-booth64.png` and `republic-of-korea-booth64.png`. For `P1`, read every file matching `/tmp/opencode/t0042/p1-*.png` numerically, and read visually the four frames that carry the mechanism claims, `p1-mech1`, `p1-mech2`, `p1-mech7`, `p1-sb`, plus the two game-launch captures `p1-sc1` and `p1-sc2`. For the 2026-11-14 side of the conflict, read numerically every file matching `/home/howard/AI/demo-evidence/t0042-h2-fp*.png` and `t0042-h2-vdmenu2.png`, and read visually `t0042-h2-fp.png` and `t0042-h2-fp3.png`.

**Files I read visually, named.** `/home/howard/AI/demo-evidence/t0042-h2-fp.png`, `/home/howard/AI/demo-evidence/t0042-h2-fp3.png`, `/tmp/opencode/t0042/p1-mech1.png`, `p1-mech2.png`, `p1-mech7.png`, `p1-sc1.png`, `p1-sb.png`, `/tmp/opencode/t0042/booth-verify-s1c-b/captures/S1b300L1-i-love-korea-f4.png`, `/tmp/opencode/t0042/S1c300L1-i-love-korea-open.png`, `S1c300L1-tux-f3.png`, `/tmp/opencode/t0042/booth-verify-s1c-b/booth-artifacts/korea-booth64.png`, `republic-of-korea-booth64.png`. Twenty-two files in total.

**Files measured numerically but not read visually, named.** All 15 `p1-*.png` (md5, dimensions, colour census), the 7 `S1b300L1-*-open.png` and 7 `S1c300L1-*-open.png`, all 52 `S1b300L1` frames, `t0042-h2-fp2.png`, `t0042-h2-vdmenu2.png`, all 10 `booth-artifacts/*booth64.png` and `i-love-korea-2line-thumbnail128.png`. **Named as not read at all:** the 31 `S1aL1`, 30 `S1bAL1` and 52 `S1b150L1` cycle frames, the 207 files under `live-segment/captures` apart from the four `l3v3-before`, `l3v3-band3_rocky`, `S1b300L1-live-demo-ice-before` and `-band3` I censused, the 17 `S1cSmokeL1` frames, the 17 `booth-artifacts/*booth32.png` and `*-mm*.png` files, `p1-cv.png`, `p1-mechcheck.png`, `p1-sb56.png`, `p1-sb7.png`, and every file in `booth-verify-d3` and `booth-verify-s1c-b` other than the paths named above.

**Method, and my control.** Every number below is mine. I ran PIL colour censuses inline through the shell and wrote no script to disk, imported no builder code, and ran no builder script. My glyph-tone figure is my own band split on the image itself, pixels with relative luminance in the 8 to 128 band counted as glyph tone against pixels at 128 or above counted as ground, because on these maps the glyph tone renders as dark navy (about 36, 40, 56) and the ground renders as light gray (176, 176, 176). On the editor cycle frames I measured only the canvas viewport rectangle `(170, 110)` to `(1790, 810)`, which I took from `p1-mech2.png` rather than from any script. **I made no contact with 192.168.1.99.** No target-side hash, mtime, process list, ERR log, flatpak prefix state or `pgrep` result in this task has been verified by me; they remain the builder's claims.

**The conflict, and my ruling.** The two records are both accurate and they describe different states of the target. **Documentation may not present the 2026-11-14 rendering evidence as current.** My ruling on which record holds is plain: **the 2026-11-22 `P1` record holds as the statement of what this target does today, and the 2026-11-14 record holds as a dated fact about what this build did once, and neither may stand alone.**

Reasons, with what I measured. The 2026-11-14 evidence is real and its own stated numbers reproduce exactly under my own independent census. `t0042-h2-fp.png` has 7885 distinct colours, the figure the 2026-11-14 record claims, and I read it as a rendered Brood War cinematic frame, rust-brown structures against pale grey, letterboxed inside a black field, 51.67 percent exact black. `t0042-h2-fp3.png` has 49974 distinct colours and I read it as the genuine StarCraft 1.16.1 main menu, `Single Player`, `Campaign Editor`, `Multiplayer`, `Exit`, `View Intro`, `Show Credits` and `Version 1.16.1` in green over a starfield with a satellite and a planet, the in-game green cursor visible near centre. `t0042-h2-fp2.png` has 43524 colours, again its record's exact claimed figure. `t0042-h2-vdmenu2.png` has exactly one colour, 2073600 pure black pixels, which reproduces the record's black-windowed-mode claim byte for byte. Nothing in `P1` refutes any of that.

The 2026-11-22 evidence is also real and it is the more recent measurement on the same build and prefix. I read `p1-sc1.png` as the plain GNOME desktop at 18:33, wallpaper and top bar only, no game surface, 42481 colours, and `p1-sc2.png` the same class at 41544 colours. The decisive control is internal to the same evening and I verified it myself: `p1-mech1.png` at 18:15 shows the `Scmdraft 2 - Select Profile` dialog with `Default` highlighted and no editor window, `p1-mech2.png` at 18:17 shows the full editor with title bar `SCmdDraft 2.0 (Beta 0.9.10) - [C:\Maps\live-demo-ice.scm ]`, the Ice canvas and status bar `Ice World\Snow`, and `p1-mech7.png` at 18:27 shows the GNOME Activities overview open with the search field and the window thumbnail labelled `Scmdraft 2.0 (Beta 0.9.10) - [C:\Maps\live-demo-ice.scm ]`. So the compositor, the session and a Wine-created window were all healthy from 18:15 to 18:29, fifteen minutes before the two StarCraft launches at 18:32:48 and 18:35:10 self-exited. That scopes the failure to the Flatpak Wine invocation, not to the target's display being down, and it is the reason I weight the later record for the current-state claim.

**One unrecorded difference between the two runs, which the "same build, same prefix" framing hides.** The 2026-11-14 launch is recorded as `flatpak run --command=wine org.winehq.Wine "C:\StarCraft\StarCraft.exe" "C:\StarCraft\testmap.scm"` at `DEMO-LOG.md:471`. The 2026-11-22 launch is recorded at `DEMO-LOG.md:2418` as the same command preceded by `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland` and `nohup`. Those are exactly the variables that govern whether a flatpak'd Wine can reach a compositor. This is a named difference, not a finding, and it is not established as the cause. It does mean the two runs are not the same invocation, so the divergence is not evidence that the target regressed. **Re-running the 2026-11-14 command line verbatim is a check no dispatch has run**, and it is the cheapest thing that could close this box before 2026-11-28. `P1`'s own not-run list already names no third launch and no windowed-mode attempt.

**What the booth may and may not say.** The intro and menu captures may be published as dated evidence with their date in the caption, and the divergence must be named beside them. They may not be used as an illustration of what the booth will show, and no sentence about StarCraft on the booth target may be written in present tense from them. The DoD playability box resting on option (c), the recorded platform limit plus per-map integrity evidence, is sound on this evidence, and I concur with closing option (b) as not testable rather than as failed: the pointer-capture hypothesis was never reached because no game surface existed, so this pass neither confirms nor refutes it.

**Findings, ranked.**

**1. A present-tense playability claim in the published docs is false on the current target.**
**Severity:** blocker.
**Where:** `DEMO-LOG.md:467` to `DEMO-LOG.md:480` for the 2026-11-14 side, `DEMO-LOG.md:2414` to `DEMO-LOG.md:2463` for the 2026-11-22 side, `## Definition of Done` playability box.
**Problem:** the only captures that show StarCraft rendering are 2026-11-14 captures, and the same build and prefix produced no window on 2026-11-22.
**Failure scenario:** `D1` writes that StarCraft runs and renders under Flatpak Wine 11.0 on the booth target, the booth operator launches it on 2026-11-28, the process exits within 12 to 37 s exactly as it did at 18:32 and 18:35 on 2026-11-22, and the published documentation is contradicted in front of an audience.
**Suggested direction:** `Vector` writes the playability section as two dated records with the divergence stated, no present-tense capability claim, and the 2026-11-14 captions carrying their date. `Tails` re-runs the verbatim 2026-11-14 command line as a bounded dispatch if the team wants option (b) reopened, and reads the resulting capture independently.

**2. A superseded non-uniform booth crop is published at the plain name, and nothing in the published record says so.**
**Severity:** should-fix.
**Where:** `booth-artifacts/korea-booth64.png` and `booth-artifacts/korea-mm.png` beside `booth-artifacts/republic-of-korea-booth64.png` and `republic-of-korea-mm.png`, manifest rows at `MANIFEST.md:43`, `:48`, `:54`, `:58`.
**Problem:** the directory carries two artifact sets for one map, and the ratified `superseded-` marking that exists for `i-love-korea`, `rocky-logo` and `rocky-with-heart` was not applied to this pair.
**Failure scenario:** I measured it. `korea-booth64.png` is an exact Lanczos downscale of `korea-mm.png`, which is 142x175, the non-square crop class `M4` measured as stretching the silhouette 23 percent and reporting 16.24 percent coverage where a uniform downscale reads 24.63. My own glyph-tone census of that file is 17.63 percent, and I read it as a squat, vertically compressed dark mass with a detached dot. `republic-of-korea-booth64.png` is an exact Lanczos downscale of the 128x128 `republic-of-korea-mm.png`, my census gives 25.00 percent glyph tone, and I read it as a correctly proportioned peninsula with a separate island. A reader picking either file from the published repo has no way to tell which is the accepted build's artifact, and the two are visually different.
**Suggested direction:** apply the ratified prefix to the 142x175-crop set or move it into `booth-artifacts/superseded/`, and re-run the manifest cross-check.

**3. Three `## Status` blocks on 2026-11-22 are stamped five to six hours before the commits that landed them.**
**Severity:** should-fix.
**Where:** the blocks stamped `2026-11-22 13:10`, `13:40` and `13:45` in `## Status`, against `git log` `0d77412` at 18:47:57, `e240ef1` at 18:49:14, `1058eb4` at 18:58:05 and `4201ef6` at 19:01:59 +0900, and `DEMO-LOG.md:2321` to `:2465` for `P1` steps 1 to 5 at 17:52 to 18:44.
**Problem:** the record's own timestamps put the `P1` outcome and the handoff before the work that produced them. Every other 2026-11-22 block matches its commit within about 15 minutes, `S1c` 11:59 against 11:50 and `V1` 12:57 against 12:47, so this is not a global clock offset.
**Failure scenario:** a reader ordering the day cannot tell whether `P1` ran before or after the 13:45 handoff, and a question that matters for finding 1, whether anything touched the flatpak prefix or the Wine state between `V1` at 12:47 and `P1` at 18:32, is unanswerable from this doc. It is also the reason `Robotnik`'s "Nothing is mid-flight, `P1` completed and is committed" at the 13:45 block cannot be checked against the log.
**Suggested direction:** restate the three stamps from the commit times and the `DEMO-LOG` entry times, which are the only clocks this task can verify, and record which clock each future stamp comes from.

**4. Every measured open frame of every deliverable map shows a blank main canvas, and the published capture set invites the opposite reading.**
**Severity:** should-fix.
**Where:** `booth-clone-s1c/captures/S1b300L1-*-open.png` and `booth-verify-s1c-b/captures/S1b300L1-*-open.png`, and the controller-side `S1c300L1-*-open.png`, described by `BOOTH-RUNBOOK.md:105` and `:177`.
**Problem:** the runbook says the maps open and render in front of the audience, and the open frames it publishes contain no map content on the canvas.
**Failure scenario:** my census on the canvas viewport rectangle. All seven `S1b300L1-*-open.png` and all seven `S1c300L1-*-open.png` measure 6 distinct colours, 93.94 to 93.99 percent ground tone, 0.02 to 0.06 percent glyph tone. `S1c300L1-i-love-korea-open.png`, which I read visually at 11:21, is a uniform snow field with the writing visible only in the 128x128 overview thumbnail at top left. Content appears only in the later frames, `S1b300L1-i-love-korea-f4.png` which I read at 25 percent zoom showing `KOREA` across the viewport at 37.88 percent glyph tone, and `S1c300L1-tux-f3.png` at 11:11 showing the tux body filling the canvas at 92.16 percent. A published caption or article sentence saying the map appears when opened is false on all fourteen open frames, and the first part of each map's display window is a blank field on the panel.
**Suggested direction:** `Vector` states the open frame as the title-bar proof it is, and the framed content frames as the audience-visible part. If the team wants the audience to see the body immediately, the runner jumps to the first framed position before the display window starts, and `S1c` re-measures.

**Severity:** nit.
**Where:** `booth-artifacts/m5-read-booth64.png`, `m5-read-booth32.png`, `m7-read-booth64.png`, `m7-read-booth32.png`, manifest rows at `MANIFEST.md:50` and `:52`.
**Problem:** names assert a size class the files do not have.

**6. Fifteen `P1` capture files exist on the controller, four of them named by no record I could find.**

**Where:** `/tmp/opencode/t0042/p1-*.png`, the `P1` inverse list at `DEMO-LOG.md:2494` to `:2498`, the dispatch brief's "eleven `P1` captures".
**Problem:** the counts do not agree and four files have no stated provenance.

A later reader cannot say which capture supports which claim, and an artifact audit against the record cannot close.
**Suggested direction:** one line per controller-side capture in the `P1` entry naming what each shows, or delete the unneeded crops.

**Checks that ran, and what they showed.** `sha256sum` aggregate over all PNGs in `booth-clone-s1c`, `booth-verify-s1c-b` and `booth-verify-d3` gives the identical aggregate `3cfaa9796bea2f74539dcc946aaaf474` and the identical path-set hash `1026f03c8bade2b0f7aa78d0188fea07` across three clones at three different commits, `dd86b46`, `93ff47b` and `f0255bd`, so the published capture and artifact set is byte-identical in all three and `S1c` added no image to it. `md5sum` pairing of the 52 `S1b300L1` frames against the 52 `S1c300L1` frames shows 52 differences, so the published-mode cycle produced its own frames rather than copies of the rebuild cycle, which is what its claim needs. `md5sum` shows `p1-mech3.png` and `p1-mech4.png` byte-identical, which independently confirms the record's zero-pixel-difference claim for the failed absolute-pointer click. My glyph-tone census of `i-love-korea-2line-thumbnail128.png` gives 31.43 percent, exactly the recorded `MTXM` coverage for the accepted build, and `tux-booth64.png` gives 67.24 percent against the recorded 67.10 percent, and `republic-of-korea-booth64.png` gives 25.00 percent against the recorded 24.16 percent, so the published thumbnail artifacts reproduce their maps' recorded coverage within 0.85 points. `PUBLISH-STATUS.md:210` to `:213` already discloses that `S1c`'s 69 capture frames live only on the controller and that no independent reader had read them; my read above covers 9 of those 69 numerically and 2 visually, which is partial coverage, not closure.

**What I could not check, named.** No target contact, so the `Errors/howard160101.ERR` entries, the flatpak prefix contents, the 12 s and 37 s process exits, the six target-side map hashes and mtimes, the 26 entries in `C:\Maps\` and the seventeen `Scm*.tmp` files are unverified by me. I have no provenance for the 2026-11-14 captures beyond their controller mtimes of 14:36:07, 14:37:58 and 14:39:50, which are fetch times, and I cannot prove they were captured on 192.168.1.99 rather than elsewhere. I ran no launch, no re-render, no `x11` or virtual-desktop attempt, and no third launch.
