## Security

*Owner: `Omega`. Read-only. Severity order.*

### One credential found in plaintext on the controller, written here by `Robotnik` under AGENTS.md section 4 (2026-11-21 18:20)

**Severity:** blocker for hygiene, no evidence of exposure beyond one mode 600 scratch file on the controller machine.
**Found by:** dispatch `D0` (`Tails`), recorded in its own `## Implementation` section with the section-ownership conflict named, because `## Security` is `Omega`'s section and `## Status` is `Robotnik`'s. AGENTS.md section 4 routes a found secret to this section and the rotation step to `## Status`, so the record is placed here by the rule rather than by ownership.
**What it is.** The target's GNOME remote-desktop credential appears as one line of `/tmp/opencode/t0042/rdp-args`, a 79 B, 6 line scratch argument file for the team's `rdp-input` and `rdp-pointer` injectors. `ls -l` reports `-rw-------` owned by `howard`, mtime `2026-11-21 10:48`. `grep -c -F -f ~/AI/secrets/scm_draft_rdp_pass.md /tmp/opencode/t0042/rdp-args` returns `1`, so exactly one line of the file is the credential, and `grep -c` against the SSH secret returns `0`.
**Where it is not.** `grep -R -l -F -f ~/AI/secrets/scm_draft_rdp_pass.md .` over the team repo working tree, 191 files scanned, returns 0 files. `git grep -l -F -f <secret> --all` over the whole team repo history returns 0. The same two checks against the SSH secret return 0. `Tails` reports `grep -rl` over a fresh clone of the booth repo returns nothing, and the booth repo tree I read from the API holds no `rdp-args` path. No planning doc, no commit, no published artifact carries it. One command of mine was wrong and I record it rather than leave it as a scare. `grep -R -c -F -f <secret> . | wc -l` returned `1724`, which counts files that grep printed a zero count for, not matches. The corrected form is `grep -R -l`, which returned 0.
**Operator action, and only the operator can take it.** The credential lives in `~/AI/secrets/scm_draft_rdp_pass.md` (mode 600) and in the target's gnome-remote-desktop credential store. Deleting `/tmp/opencode/t0042/rdp-args` removes the copy and does not rotate the credential. Rotation is `grdctl` on 192.168.1.99 followed by a fresh secret file, and it interacts with `R1` to `R5` and with TASK-0041 hygiene item 2, the pre-existing world-readable `credentials.ini` on the target, so the two should be decided together. `Omega` rules the 3389 listener and the listener's credential posture in `R2`, and this finding belongs in that ruling.
**Related open hygiene item, re-verified today.** `ls -l ~/AI/secrets/` shows `scm_draft_pass.md` at `-rw-r--r--`, mode 644, where AGENTS.md section 4 requires 600. That is TASK-0041 `## Status` hygiene item 1, still unfixed, and it is a permissions change the operator can make in one command without touching the target.

### R2 security read (2026-11-22, `Omega`, second in the review chain)

Read-only. No target contact, no contact with any live service, no credential value read or printed. Modes were read by path only. Commands that produced each claim are named with it. Findings in severity order.

**Ruling on the items `R2` was asked to rule on, in one block so the fix pass can work top-down.** COPR `forecastwolf157/Wine-test`, high (finding 4), disable it now with the inverse already recorded. Flatpak Wine from Flathub, medium (finding 5), provenance is better than the COPR, the open question is the sandbox boundary and it is a target-side read that has not run. Target repo set `baseos`, `appstream`, `extras`, medium (finding 4), that set is not the set the target actually holds. The 3389 listener with its self-signed certificate, high (findings 1 and 2), the certificate is not the problem, the fact that neither channel authenticates the server is. Target-side residue, low (finding 9), keeping it named is right, the username path in the title bar is the part that needs a decision. The plaintext RDP credential file, medium (finding 8), mode is correct and the location and lifetime are not. `scm_draft_pass.md` at 644, medium (finding 10), one command, still unfixed, verified today. The three TASK-0041 hygiene items, findings 3, 7 and 10. Unsigned team commits, medium (finding 11), with a correction, the two packaging commits are signed.

**1. SSH host key verification is switched off in the packaged tooling while a password credential is handed to the connection**

**Severity:** high
**Vector:** authz
**Where:** `scripts/remote/rt-lib:29`, `RT_SSH_OPTS=(-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=10)`; the same posture in the booth runner at `/tmp/opencode/t0042/booth_loop.py:83-84`, `SSH = ["sshpass", "-f", SSH_PASS, "ssh", "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=no", HOST]`. Verified today, `grep -rn 'StrictHostKeyChecking' scripts tests .github` returns `rt-lib:29` and `scripts/vm-create:147` (the vm-create one is `accept-new`, which is fine).
**Attack:** who controls the input, the network between the controller and the target. TASK-0041 `## Status` Unknowns item 4 records the booth network as assumed same LAN and never verified, and a conference LAN is not a LAN the team controls. With verification off, anything positioned on that path can answer the controller's connection to 192.168.1.99 with its own host key, and `sshpass -f` then hands it the target SSH password verbatim, and every subsequent command the runner issues is executed by whoever answered.
**Impact:** the target SSH credential, and arbitrary execution as `howard` on the machine the audience watches. `howard` on that target has passwordless sudo (`DEMO-LOG.md:2335`, `sudo -n true` answers 0 and `sudo -n python3` runs), so that is root on the booth machine, which makes findings 3, 7 and 9 reachable from a network position rather than only from local access.
**Fix:** pin the target host key. Seed a controller-side known-hosts file once from the verified LAN target, set `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=<that file>` in `RT_SSH_OPTS` and in `booth_loop.py`'s `SSH` and `SCP` lists, and add a selftest assert that no file under `scripts/` contains `StrictHostKeyChecking=no`, which is cheap and needs no target.

**2. `/cert:ignore` is baked into the RDP argument template, so the channel that carries the plaintext RDP credential never authenticates the server**

**Severity:** high
**Vector:** authz
**Where:** `scripts/remote/rt-lib:155` (dry-run form) and `scripts/remote/rt-lib:161` (real form), both emit `/cert:ignore` as part of the argument lines. The target side is a self-signed certificate the team generated itself (`DEMO-LOG.md:112-118`) and whose private key sits at `~/.config/gnome-remote-desktop/tls-key.pem`, mode 600, owner `howard` (`DEMO-LOG.md:116-118`, key stays 600, cert is chmod 644).
**Attack:** same network position as finding 1. The client is told in advance to accept any certificate, so the TLS layer proves nothing about who is answering 3389, and the RDP credential travels to whoever it is. Unlike SSH, the RDP credential is the credential for the live session itself.
**Impact:** the RDP credential plus a live input channel into the demo session. With `lock-enabled` false (finding 7), input from that channel lands directly on the unlocked desktop the audience is watching, so the impact is not only a stolen credential but a hijacked booth.
**Fix:** ranked recommendation. First, stop exposing 3389 at the venue at all, tunnel it over the SSH connection (`ssh -L 127.0.0.1:3399:127.0.0.1:3389` on the controller, point `rdp-input` and `rdp-pointer` at 127.0.0.1) and remove the source-restricted rich rule from finding 4. That removes both this finding and finding 4 in one change, and it reuses the channel that finding 1's fix has already authenticated. Second, if 3389 must stay reachable from the venue network, replace `/cert:ignore` in the template with a pinned certificate thumbprint for the target and record the pin, then add a selftest assert that no credential-bearing tool emits `cert:ignore`.

**3. The team made a world-readable copy of the pre-existing grd credentials file on the target, recorded as "no inverse"**

**Severity:** high
**Vector:** secrets
**Where:** `DEMO-LOG.md:100-103`, `sudo mkdir -p /home/howard/AI/demo-backup/2026-11-13` then `sudo cp -a /var/lib/gnome-remote-desktop/.local/share/gnome-remote-desktop ... /home/howard/AI/demo-backup/2026-11-13/grd-credentials.ini`, labelled "Backup (no inverse, additive)". The source file's mode is recorded at `DEMO-LOG.md:97-99` as 644 plaintext. `cp -a` preserves mode, and `sudo mkdir -p` yields a 755 root-owned directory, so the copy is a world-readable plaintext credential inside a world-listable directory on the target's `/home`.
**Attack:** any local account on the target, or any code that lands as `howard`. The second path is not hypothetical in this task's own file set: the editor parses third-party binary map containers, and `(2)River Crossing.scm`, a shipped protected third-party map, is in the set the team launches (`DEMO-LOG.md:743`).
**Impact:** a credential whose origin and scope the team never established, on the machine the audience stands next to, readable by anyone local. Combined with finding 1 or 5 it is a step to root.
**Fix:** ruling on TASK-0041 hygiene item 2, stated as my recommendation. The live half of that item is already closed by the team, the pre-existing credential was overwritten by `grdctl rdp clear-credentials` plus `set-credentials` (`DEMO-LOG.md:99-100`), so what remains is the copy. Concrete action for the fix pass, on the target, either delete `grd-credentials.ini` in the backup directory (the value it preserves is no longer the live value) or `chmod 600` it and move it under a 0700 directory, and record whichever is done with its inverse. Then rotate the current RDP credential after the event, which is the operator's step already recorded at `:4479`. Not verified by me, no target contact.

**4. 3389 is source-restricted to 192.168.1.102, an address the controller will not hold at the venue, and the target's enabled repo set is wider than the record states**

**Severity:** medium
**Vector:** authz plus supply-chain (two records that both describe the booth machine's posture, grouped because the fix pass touches them in the same target pass)
**Where:** firewall, `DEMO-LOG.md:131-135`, one rich rule `source address="192.168.1.102" port port="3389" protocol="tcp" accept`, `--list-ports` empty. Repos, `DEMO-LOG.md:218-219`, `DEMO-LOG.md:221` and `DEMO-LOG.md:237`, which records "Final repos on target: `baseos`, `appstream`, `extras`, `crb`, `copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:forecastwolf157:Wine-test`". The narrower `baseos`, `appstream`, `extras` statement in TASK-0041 `## Status` is the state at 2026-11-13 and does not describe the machine today.
**Attack (firewall):** on 2026-11-28 the controller will not be 192.168.1.102. Either the loop cannot connect and the booth stalls, or whoever unblocks it at the booth widens the rule to the venue subnet or drops the source restriction, which puts the unauthenticated-by-default listener from finding 2 on a conference network with an unlocked desktop from finding 7. The dangerous branch is the one that happens under time pressure at the booth.
**Attack (repos):** whoever controls the COPR project `forecastwolf157/Wine-test`, or the account that owns it, publishes a new build. The next `dnf` transaction on the booth machine can install it with no review, no pin and no version hold. The package is a Wine Staging build, `wine-10.17-1.el10.x86_64` (`DEMO-LOG.md:221`), whose job on that machine is to parse map containers.
**Impact:** firewall branch, exposure of 3389 to a network the team does not control. Repo branch, code execution as `howard` from a supply-chain position the team chose to keep open, and `howard` has passwordless sudo. Honest bound on the repo branch: package integrity is verifiable, the COPR key is recorded at `DEMO-LOG.md:237` as `gpg-pubkey-465fccc2-68bd0e9e`, so this is trust placement and mutability, not unsigned packages.
**Fix:** firewall, decide the booth-day shape before the event and record it, preferably by adopting the tunnel in finding 2 and removing the 192.168.1.102 rule entirely, otherwise record a rule scoped to the venue subnet in advance rather than improvising on 2026-11-28. Repos, run the inverses that are already recorded, `sudo dnf copr disable -y forecastwolf157/Wine-test` (`DEMO-LOG.md:219`) and `sudo dnf config-manager --set-disabled crb` (`DEMO-LOG.md:218`), the packages are installed so the repos are no longer needed, then record `rpm -q wine` and `rpm -K wine` as booth-evidence before the event. Wherever a document states the target repo set, state the set the target actually holds.

**5. Flatpak Wine from Flathub is the build that renders, and its sandbox boundary against the grd key pair is unread**

**Severity:** medium
**Vector:** supply-chain, with an authz consequence
**Where:** `DEMO-LOG.md:467-476` (Flatpak Wine 11.0 renders the intro and menu where the COPR build shows black), `DEMO-LOG.md:508-509` (Flathub user remote added, `flatpak install -y flathub org.winehq.Wine/x86_64/wow64-25.08`, inverse `flatpak --user remote-delete flathub` recorded).
**Attack and consequence:** provenance here is better than the COPR, `org.winehq.Wine` is the upstream WineHQ Flathub application and flatpak verifies it against its own key, so I do not rule this as a supply-chain risk in the same way as finding 4. What I do rule on is the boundary. Flatpak confinement is not a security boundary for an application that needs the user's files, and Wine needs a home directory for its prefix. The target's RDP TLS private key and the grd credential store are inside `~/.config/gnome-remote-desktop/`, which is inside the home directory. If the flatpak carries home-wide filesystem access, then a Wine-hosted process parsing a map container can read the RDP TLS private key and the credential store, which is a path from a document-parse bug to RDP session decryption or authentication without ever touching the network.
**Impact:** the credential and the TLS key behind the listener in findings 1, 2 and 4.
**Fix:** `flatpak info --show-permissions org.winehq.Wine` on the target and record the output, that is the check that decides this finding. Then run the booth demo as a dedicated `booth` account whose home holds the Wine prefix and the maps and holds no grd credential and no TLS key. The dedicated account is also the single change that improves findings 3, 7 and 9 at once, so I recommend it over any per-file permission fix. Also record which Wine the booth runs, two builds and two prefixes on a booth machine is an operational ambiguity that becomes a security ambiguity when a prefix is the thing that holds credentials.

**6. `lock-enabled` went `true` to `false` on the machine the audience stands next to**

**Severity:** medium, needs a recorded accept-or-fix decision
**Vector:** authz
**Where:** `DEMO-LOG.md:136-137`, with the inverse recorded, and TASK-0041 `## Status` hygiene item 3. `org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay` was already `uint32 0`, so nothing re-locks on its own.
**Attack:** anyone who walks up to the booth laptop during a display window has an unlocked live session as `howard`. `howard` has passwordless sudo. Physical presence at an open booth is therefore root on the target, with no credential and no network required.
**Impact:** read every map and every credential in `howard`'s home, run anything, or break the cycle mid-demo in front of the audience.
**Fix:** my recommendation, run the booth as a dedicated non-sudo `booth` account (finding 5), which turns an unlocked session into an unlocked sandbox rather than an unlocked path to root. If the operator keeps the demo on `howard`, then keep `lock-enabled=false` only for the duration of a cycle and re-lock it in the runner's teardown, the inverse is already recorded at `DEMO-LOG.md:137`. Either way the decision belongs in `## Status` before 2026-11-28 rather than as an open item.

**7. Remote command strings are built by interpolation and `rt-shot --name` is unvalidated**

**Severity:** medium
**Vector:** input-validation
**Where:** `scripts/remote/rt-shot:36-37`, `TARGET_PATH="${RT_TARGET_TMP}/${NAME}"` and `shot_cmd="$(rt_session_env) ${RT_SCREENSHOT_BIN} -f ${TARGET_PATH}"`, then `rt-shot:47` and `rt-shot:56` pass `"$shot_cmd"` through `rt_ssh`, and `scripts/remote/rt-lib:111` hands the whole string to the target's shell as one argument. `NAME` comes from `--name` with no validation at all (`rt-shot:33-38`). Same shape in `scripts/remote/rt-uinput` (`run_cmd="sudo -n ${REMOTE_BIN}"` composed by concatenation and passed to `rt_ssh`), in `/tmp/opencode/t0042/booth_loop.py:198`, `tscript(f"bash /tmp/t0042-run-dos.sh '{dos_path}'")`, and in `booth_loop.py:179`, `remote = f"/tmp/{tag}.png"`.
**Attack:** the values are not always team-authored. SCMDraft generates backup and map names itself, this target's file set already carries a name with a space and parentheses, `(2)River Crossing.scm` (`DEMO-LOG.md:743`), and a `.scm` container's internal name comes from whoever built the map. A name carrying a single quote, a semicolon or a command substitution becomes commands executed on the target as `howard`, and in `rt-uinput`'s case under `sudo -n`, so as root.
**Impact:** arbitrary execution on the target as `howard`, as root where the composed string sits in a `sudo -n` command. Honest bound, today the booth opens team-built maps with names this task chose, and a bare `(` only breaks the command rather than running anything, which is why this is medium and not high. The mechanism is what the fix pass must close, not a live exploit.
**Fix:** validate `NAME` against an allowlist such as `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.png$` and reject everything else, quote every interpolated value with `printf '%q'` in the shell tools and `shlex.quote` in `booth_loop.py`, and add a selftest assert that a hostile `--name` is refused under `--dry-run` with no target, which the existing dry-run block already supports.

**8. The booth runner makes a persistent plaintext credential file in a world-listable `/tmp` path a preflight requirement**

**Severity:** medium
**Vector:** secrets
**Where:** verified today by path only, `stat -c '%a %U:%G %n'` gives `600 howard:howard /tmp/opencode/t0042/rdp-args`, and `stat` gives `755 /tmp/opencode` and `755 /tmp/opencode/t0042`. The requirement is in `/tmp/opencode/t0042/booth_loop.py:549` and `:552-553`, which fail preflight with `RDP args file missing` when the file is absent, with `INJECTOR_DIR` defaulting to `/tmp/opencode/t0042` (`booth_loop.py:65`).
**Attack:** the mode protects the content, so the exposure is the lifetime and the location. A credential file sits in a shared, world-listable directory for the whole task lifetime, it survives every dispatch teardown that claims to remove it (`DEMO-LOG.md:438` and `DEMO-LOG.md:516-517` both record creating and deleting these files, and the file is present today), and it is inside whatever snapshots, collects or backs up `/tmp`. Anyone with a local account on the controller learns the path exists and can attempt to read it, and anyone who lands any code as `howard` on the controller reads it without effort.
**Impact:** the target RDP credential, which finding 2 shows is the credential for the audience-facing session.
**Fix:** the packaged tooling already has the right pattern. `scripts/remote/rt-click` builds the args file with `mktemp` under `umask 077`, `chmod 600` and a `trap` cleanup, and `scripts/remote/rt-lib:11-13` states that the scripts create no credential file at all. Move `INJECTOR_DIR` to a 0700 directory under the operator's own tree, generate the args file at cycle start and delete it in the cycle teardown, and drop the preflight requirement for a persistent file so the runner follows the tooling rather than replacing it. This is not a rotation question, rotation of the underlying credential is the operator's step already recorded at `:4479`.

**9. Target-side residue is audience-visible on the panel, and the capture residue is world-listable on the booth machine**

**Severity:** low
**Vector:** input-validation is not the vector here, this is disclosure, so authz with a documentation consequence
**Where:** the seventeen `Scm*.tmp` backups at 9845475 B, `live-demo-ice.scm` at 12502 B, `(2)River Crossing.scm` at 90426 B, the 1152 B error file `Errors/howard160101.ERR`, and 7195615 B per cycle of capture PNGs in the target's `/tmp`. The capture path is the default `RT_TARGET_TMP=/tmp` (`rt-lib:27`) and `booth_loop.py:179`. None of these are verified by me, no target contact.
**Attack:** the disclosure path is the title bar, which this task proved three times carries the map path (the `M5` carried fact and the withdrawn `M4` finding 6). On a 1920x1080 panel facing an audience, a viewer reads `/home/howard/...`, the third-party map name `(2)River Crossing.scm`, and the scratch name `live-demo-ice.scm`, and the error file name carries the target username. The `/tmp` PNGs are full-frame captures of the demo session, listable by any local account on a machine standing in an open booth, and they hold whatever was on screen at capture time, including any credential prompt or terminal window.
**Impact:** the operator's username and the controller's directory shape become part of the audience-facing display, and full-screen captures of the demo session accumulate on the booth machine. Disk capacity is not the finding, roughly 21 MB across three cycles against 64 G free is bounded.
**Fix:** keeping the residue named rather than hidden is correct and I am not asking for deletion, rule r002 stands. Three concrete changes instead, point `RT_TARGET_TMP` and the runner's capture path at a 0700 scratch directory rather than `/tmp`, add a teardown step that lists the capture files with sizes and removes them after the final cycle, and decide explicitly whether a title bar reading `/home/howard/...` is acceptable on a public booth display. Renaming the residue is the only way to change what a viewer reads, so if the answer is no, that is a rename decision, not a cleanup decision.

**10. The controller SSH secret is still mode 644, and the packaged tool only warns about it**

**Severity:** medium
**Vector:** secrets
**Where:** verified today by path only, `stat` gives `644 howard:howard /home/howard/AI/secrets/scm_draft_pass.md`. AGENTS.md section 4 requires 600. `scripts/remote/rt-lib:79-96` reads the mode and emits a warning rather than refusing, and the comment at `rt-lib:81-83` names this exact file and its exact mode as a known open item.
**Attack and honest bound:** on this controller the parent directory `/home/howard/AI/secrets` is mode 700, verified today, and that is what actually keeps other non-root users out today, not the file mode. So this is not exploitable on the machine as it stands by any other-user path I can construct, which is why it is medium and not high. What it is, is one directory-mode change, one backup, one copy into a shared path, or one `rsync` away from being a plaintext world-readable SSH password for a machine with passwordless sudo, and AGENTS.md section 4 does not permit the 644 state regardless.
**Impact:** the target SSH password, which finding 1 shows is a path to root on the target.

Two follow-ups for the fix pass, decide whether `rt_require_secret_file` should fail rather than warn for a booth run, and add a selftest assert on the mode of each `~/AI/secrets` file the tooling reads, which needs no target and no credential value.

**11. Three unsigned team commits carry this task's own security evidence, and the packaging record that was handed to me is wrong about two more**

**Severity:** medium
**Vector:** supply-chain, record integrity
**Where:** verified today with `git log -1 --format='%G?'`, `8e75aac` `N`, `d26ef2b` `N`, `5f9947d` `N`. Against 60 commits on `main` the split is 57 `G` and 3 `N`, so the three are the exception, not the rule. `git config --get commit.gpgsign` returns `true` locally and `true` globally today, so the cause the record names (`DEMO-LOG.md:2010`, `commit.gpgsign=false` for the D3 dispatch) is closed in configuration now.
**What is exposed by them:** the D3 staging record, the runbook claim-source record, and the credential scan result. The claim "no credential in any git path" and the runbook's claim-source table rest on commits a consumer cannot tie to the key the rest of the chain uses, which is the weakest possible place to have an unsigned commit, the security evidence itself.
**Correction to the brief I was dispatched with, and it matters to the fix pass.** `b906f00` and `1eea4ec` are not unsigned. `git log -1 --format='%G? %GK'` returns `G F9261D151316FD60` for both, the same key as the signed majority. The packaging pass recorded them as unsigned, that record is wrong, and correcting the record is the action. Re-signing them is not needed and rewriting history is not warranted.
**Two further verified facts about the chain.** The team signing key `F9261D151316FD60` is ed25519 with no expiry field in the keyring (`gpg --list-keys --with-colons`), so no signed commit ages into an expired state. The booth repo's root commit `7e0d58d` verifies as `E`, a good signature from key `B5690EEEBB952194`, which is GitHub's web-signing key, so the root of the published booth chain is signed by GitHub rather than by the team. Every booth commit above it, `3da0937`, `39f2119`, `f0255bd`, `dd86b46`, `0f31e96` and `93ff47b`, verifies `G` against the team key in all three clones I hold under `/tmp/opencode/t0042`. That root state is low severity on its own and worth explaining rather than leaving a consumer to find an unexplained `E`.
**Fix:** no history rewriting. Add a signed attestation, a signed tag at `5f9947d` from the team key plus one signed commit naming `8e75aac`, `d26ef2b` and `5f9947d` with their tree hashes, so the evidence those commits carry is bound to the key. Correct the packaging record in place. Publish a signed tag at the booth repo tip so the chain from the published tip upward is all team-signed. Record in `## Status` that `commit.gpgsign=false` caused the lapse and is now `true`.

**12. A PR body is interpolated straight into a `run:` body on a public repository**

**Severity:** high, currently unreachable because of one precondition named below
**Vector:** actions
**Where:** `.github/workflows/planning-doc-gate.yml:29`, `pr_body="${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}"`, inside a `run:` block. `grep -rn 'github.event' .github/workflows` finds this as the only such interpolation today.
**Attack:** anyone on the internet. The repo is public by operator decision, and AGENTS.md section 8 says PRs within `metalllinux` need no human review, so the body is untrusted input that the runner substitutes into a shell script before bash sees it. A body carrying a quote and a semicolon executes the attacker's commands on the runner, which is the operator's own machine.
**Impact:** arbitrary execution on the runner. Honest bound on exploitability, today it is unreachable, because GitHub does not allow self-hosted runner registration on a public repository and this repo's runner is not registered (AGENTS.md section 6), so the job has no runner to land on. That single precondition is the only thing between this finding and execution on the operator's machine, and it disappears the moment the repo goes private.
**Fix:** bind it, add `env: PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}` at job or step level and read `"$PR_BODY"` in the script. Add a selftest or CI assert that no `run:` body in `.github/workflows` contains a `github.event.*` expression, which is a grep and needs no runner.

**Severity:** low
**Vector:** supply-chain, actions
**Where:** `uses: actions/checkout@v4` at `deploy.yml:54`, `deploy.yml:75`, `planning-doc-gate.yml:23`, `secret-scan.yml:25`, `secret-scan.yml:41` and `test-runner.yml:63`. `static-checks.yml:24` uses `@v4` with only a comment naming a SHA. `licence-check.yml:40` and `team-selftest.yml:28` are the compliant form, `actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2`. **14. The selftest credential gate checks one credential, in the working tree only, and it can pass by not running**

**Severity:** medium
**Vector:** secrets
**Where:** `tests/selftest.sh:220-231`. It greps `.` with `--exclude-dir=.git` against `scm_draft_pass.md` only, and at `:231` it records "credential leak scan skipped" and passes when the secret file is absent. Neither `scm_draft_rdp_pass.md` nor `token.md` is in the gate, and nothing in the gate looks at commit history.
**Attack:** a credential reaching a committed planning doc or artifact. If it is the RDP password or the GitHub token, the local gate that AGENTS.md section 6 makes the effective CI gate does not notice, and if the secret file is ever moved out of the way the gate turns green by skipping.
**Impact:** the effective local gate would pass a real leak of two of the three credentials this task depends on.
**Fix:** extend the scan to both target credential files and to `token.md`, add a history form alongside the working-tree form (`git grep -lF -f <secret> -- $(git rev-list HEAD)`, or rely on `gitleaks` with `fetch-depth: 0`, which `secret-scan.yml:26` already configures for the workflow side), and make an absent secret file a failure or an explicit skip marker rather than a note that reads as a pass. Checks I ran that show the current state is clean, `grep -RIlFf` over the team repo working tree for the SSH secret returns 0 files, `git grep -lF` over the last 300 commits of `HEAD` for both target credentials returns nothing, and the same working-tree scan against `/tmp/opencode/t0042/booth-verify-s1c-b` and `booth-verify-d3` returns 0 matches. Matching by path only, no value printed.

**15. License signals, carried for the chain rather than ruled**

**Severity:** low

**Findings. Each one with the fix Tails must make, and the two that need the operator.**

C1, licence declaration conflict inside the team repo, Tails. `scripts/rdp-pointer.c` carries the header line `License: Apache-2.0 (links against libfreerdp3 / libfreerdp-client3, Apache-2.0)`, `scripts/rdp-input.c` inherits that claim from rdp-pointer, `scripts/remote/NOTICE` states the team C tools are "Apache-2.0, under the repository root licence (LICENSE at repo root)", and `team/licenses/policy.yaml` states "Team Chaotix itself is Apache-2.0". The root `LICENSE` is MIT. Three claims and the file disagree. Nothing imported imposes copyleft, StormLib is MIT, FreeRDP is taken under Apache-2.0, Natural Earth is public domain, the 110 m record is dedicated, so either direction is lawful and the fix is to pick one and align, my recommendation MIT at the root with MIT headers in `scripts/rdp-input.c`, `scripts/rdp-pointer.c` and `scripts/remote/uinput-inject.c` (which carries no licence header at all, a missing-attribution finding), then the NOTICE and policy lines restated to match. Do not relicense any inherited copyleft, there is none here.

C2, the Rocky Linux mark is published in the booth tree, operator decision. The booth tree holds `maps/deliverable/rocky-logo.scm`, `maps/deliverable/rocky-with-heart.scm`, 13 `booth-artifacts/*rocky-logo*` and `*rocky-with-heart*` renders, and 20-plus `captures/` frames of the same mark as the editor draws it. The mask geometry is rasterized from the shipped distro SVG (`code/rocky_svg.py:1-8`), and the licence that ships with that asset grants use "only during the normal operation of software programs that call upon the Package. No other copyright or trademark license is granted herein." A public GitHub repository that publishes renders of the mark is not that use. The three lawful alternatives, in my recommended order, (a) keep the repo private as it is, (b) publish with the two Rocky-mark maps and their renders and captures removed, `MANIFEST.md` naming the removal, (c) obtain the Rocky Linux Foundation's logo usage approval before publishing. I do not grant the exception, this is the operator's call, and it is written here for `Robotnik` to fold into `## Status` because it is not my section to edit.

C3, the published captures and maps are renders of Blizzard content, operator decision, and this is the plain ruling on the public flip. Facts first. `PUBLISH-STATUS.md:156` states it itself, "The captures and booth artifacts that landed are downscaled renders of Blizzard tileset tones." The era-6 reference the four silhouette maps and the live seed are built from is a Blizzard campaign map's CHK with the `ERA ` word patched to 6 (`DEMO-LOG.md:845`), and 164 `.chk` extracts of Blizzard maps sit on the controller outside git (`DEMO-LOG.md:843`). The captures are frames the SCMDraft 2 editor drew, and SCMDraft 2 itself publishes no licence grant at all (`All content copyright © 2001-2019 Stormcoast Fortress`). The maps the team wrote are its own authorship, and their terrain arrays are the team's masks, but the container skeleton they reuse comes from a Blizzard map. Ruling stated plainly: the exclusion rule is satisfied and the gate passes, and that is not the same as the captures clearing a public flip. Public visibility of 341 `captures/` files plus 207 `live-segment/captures/` files plus 73 `booth-artifacts/` files is a distribution act covering renders of Blizzard tileset art, renders of a closed editor's UI, and the Rocky mark, and C2 and C3 must both be resolved by the operator before the flip. The operator's acceptance recorded 2026-11-22 22:10 UTC covers the tree's contents against the two named classes, and it does not read as a decision on public distribution of those renders.

C4, the Ar3sgice mirror carries no licence file upstream, verified at tree `00b5fb512d475420b8f50715978ad4a0394d2937`, and the team downloaded one of its binaries (`bmp2scx1.0.rar`, extracted at doc:1753). Nothing from it is published, so the house hard stop `no_licence` is not engaged in any repo. The standing rule that follows for `D1`: name the mirror as a source with its ref, and carry no binary from it. `colorbase.bin` stays withheld.

C5, record correction, mine to make because it is a licence fact and the record contradicts itself. `doc:744` records StormLib as "MIT, `github.com/ladislav-zezula/StormLib` at `d60b7e6d3501474f4d92c7b9c752a37e78385f67`". `doc:1796` records StormLib as "Freeware (not open-source)". At the ref actually used the repo carries `LICENSE`, blob `2cb432d4ec85706acfb1a606bcc010a70b96ed86`, and that text is the MIT License. `doc:744` is right and `doc:1796` is wrong for that ref. No other agent's section is edited here, this line is the correction.

C6, the booth repo has no NOTICE file. It publishes 94 code files, 13 maps, 548 capture files and 73 artifacts, and its only licence file is the root MIT `LICENSE`. StormLib is named in `README.md`, `MANIFEST.md` and `PUBLISH-STATUS.md` and the pinned commit is not stated in the repo. Fix for Tails, add a booth-repo `NOTICE` naming StormLib MIT at `d60b7e6d3501474f4d92c7b9c752a37e78385f67`, Natural Earth public domain at tag `v5.1.2` commit `f1890d9f152c896d250a77557a5751a93d494776`, the 110 m record's `UNLICENSE` dedication, `rocky-logos-100.5-3.el10` with its usage restriction quoted, and the SCMDraft 2 and StarCraft facts, then regenerate the `MANIFEST.md` row for it. **Ruling on `Omega` finding 12, the PR body interpolated into a `run:` body.** I confirm the finding exactly as written, and it is unfixed at HEAD. `.github/workflows/planning-doc-gate.yml:29` is still `pr_body="${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}"` inside a `run:` block, verified by `sed -n '29p'` and by `grep -rn 'github.event' .github/workflows`, which returns that one line. The severity stands at high with the same honest bound `Omega` gave, GitHub does not register a self-hosted runner on a public repo, so the job has no runner to land on today, and that is the only thing between this line and execution on the operator's machine. My addition to the ruling: the fix is not only a line change, it is also the missing gate. `Omega` asked for a selftest assert that no `run:` body contains a `github.event.*` expression, that assert does not exist (row above), so the class is unguarded as well as unfixed, and the repo going private would remove the sole precondition without any local gate noticing. Two further instances of the same interpolation class that the finding does not name, `deploy.yml:40`, `:44`, `:86` and `:87` place `workflow_call` and `workflow_dispatch` inputs directly into `run:` bodies (`${{ inputs.confirm }}` sits inside a shell `[ ... ]` test, which is the same substitution mechanism), and AGENTS.md section 6 requires inputs to be bound to `env:`. `licence-check.yml:50` shows the compliant form already in this repo. My call, bind `PR_BODY` and the `deploy.yml` inputs to `env:` and add the grep assert to `tests/selftest.sh` in one `Tails` pass, before any visibility flip. This is a code finding, it goes to `Tails`.

**Ruling on `Omega` finding 13, `actions/checkout` unpinned.** I confirm it and I widen it. Unpinned `actions/checkout@v4` occurs at 7 sites, `deploy.yml:54`, `deploy.yml:75`, `planning-doc-gate.yml:23`, `secret-scan.yml:25`, `secret-scan.yml:41`, `test-runner.yml:63`, and `test-runner.yml:86`. `Omega` named six and missed `test-runner.yml:86`. An eighth case is a pseudo-pin, `static-checks.yml:24` reads `uses: actions/checkout@v4 # SHA: 08c6903`, a comment is not a pin and a 7-hex-digit fragment cannot be resolved, so that site reads compliant and is not. `secret-scan-self.yml` adds no site of its own but inherits the unpinned ref through `uses: ./.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml`. Only `licence-check.yml:40` and `team-selftest.yml:28` carry the pinned form `actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2`. Severity stays low, mutable tag on GitHub's own org with no runner to execute it, and the fix is mechanical, copy the two compliant lines. `Tails` work.

**Harness bug I found, mine to fix, not a code bug.** The count floor in `.github/workflows/team-selftest.yml:44` to `:55` does not work. `grep -Eo '[0-9]+ checks passed' | grep -o '^[0-9]'` keeps the first digit only, so a run reporting `105 checks passed` yields `COUNT=1`, and `[ 1 -lt 70 ]` is true, so the step would print `selftest reported 1 checks; expected at least 70` and exit 1 against a passing suite. I reproduced it on the literal string. Two consequences. Had CI ever run, this step would have failed every green run since the count crossed 100, and any count whose leading digit is 7 or higher would pass the floor whatever its true size. The floor is also stale, `MIN=70` against a 105 baseline, 35 checks of slack. And the floor lives only in a CI job that has never executed, while the effective local gate, `scripts/hooks/pre-push` (present, mode 755, `core.hooksPath` set), runs `tests/selftest.sh` and asserts nothing about the count, since `tests/selftest.sh:286` only prints it. So the AGENTS.md section 18 claim that CI asserts a minimum check count is currently unenforced end to end. Fix, `grep -Eo '^[0-9]+'` instead of `grep -o '^[0-9]'`, raise `MIN` to a value near the baseline, and move the count assert into `tests/selftest.sh` so the gate that actually runs is the one that asserts.
